content.value_statement: Poor schema choices cause slow queries, data duplication, and risky migrations. This skill guides SQL and NoSQL schema design, indexing, relationships, and migration planning.
actual_capabilities: Collects database type, domain, entities, expected volume, and read/write patterns.
Maps entities to attributes, keys, data types, and table relationships.
Produces ERD guidance with Mermaid-style relationship notation.
Recommends normalization, denormalization, indexes, constraints, and triggers.
Drafts migration structure with up and down steps for schema changes.
Provides MongoDB collection design and indexing examples.
limitations: Does not inspect live database statistics or query plans by itself.
Generated schemas need review against business rules and compliance needs.
Examples may require database-specific syntax changes before use.
Does not run migrations or validate SQL without separate tools.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product Schema
use_cases.description: Create tables, keys, and relationships for an application before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Slow Database
use_cases.description: Identify normalization, indexing, and relationship changes that can reduce query latency.

use_cases.title: Document a Data Model
use_cases.description: Produce ERD notes, table descriptions, and migration structure for team review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Schema
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new application database.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a database schema for a new application. Use PostgreSQL. The domain is [domain]. The main entities are [entities]. Include tables, keys, and relationships.

prompt_templates.title: Add Relationships and Indexes
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request after core entities are known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this schema for relationship integrity and query performance. Add foreign keys, junction tables, unique constraints, and indexes for these query patterns: [queries].

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for changing an existing schema.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan for this schema change: [change]. Include up steps, down steps, data backfill notes, locking risks, and rollback concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Complex Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for scale, consistency, and operational risk.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this database design for a production system with [volume] records and [traffic pattern]. Assess normalization, indexes, constraints, partitioning, migration risk, and data security.

output_examples.input: Design a PostgreSQL schema for an e-commerce app with users, products, orders, and reviews.
output_examples.output: A normalized schema plan with user, product, order, order item, category, and review tables. It includes keys, relationships, indexes, and migration notes.

output_examples.input: Plan a MongoDB schema for a high-read chat application.
output_examples.output: A collection design for users, conversations, and messages. It explains denormalized fields, participant indexes, message history access, and read-performance tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Review an existing schema that has slow joins and inconsistent foreign keys.
output_examples.output: A review summary that identifies missing indexes, weak constraints, relationship gaps, and safe migration steps for applying fixes.

best_practices: Provide the database engine, expected scale, query patterns, and relationship rules.
Review generated keys, constraints, and indexes against real business rules.
Ask for migration steps and rollback notes before production changes.
anti_patterns: Requesting schema output without explaining entities or relationships.
Copying example migrations directly into production without testing.
Adding indexes for every column without clear query evidence.

faq.question: Which databases does this skill support?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, SQLite, and similar SQL or NoSQL systems.

faq.question: Can it generate migration plans?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline up steps, down steps, rollback concerns, and data backfill notes.

faq.question: Does it run database commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance and examples. It does not execute migrations or database queries by itself.

faq.question: Can it help with indexing strategy?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends indexes based on query patterns, joins, uniqueness needs, and read or write tradeoffs.

faq.question: Is it useful for NoSQL modeling?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes MongoDB collection design, denormalization guidance, and indexing examples.

faq.question: What should I provide for best results?
faq.answer: Provide the database type, entities, relationships, expected volume, query patterns, and transaction requirements.
